bull_bear.body:
- Business revival uncertainty and operating at sub-optimal levels — The company is in the process of business revival with the Sahibabad unit working much below optimum level and the Sonepat unit closed, indicating severe operational and financial distress.
- Significant decline in production and sales — Production fell from 29,456 to 21,838 bicycles and sales dropped from â¹1,714 lacs to â¹690 lacs, reflecting a sharp contraction in core operations and market presence.
- Pending corporate insolvency applications — Two insolvency applications totaling â¹10.51 crores are pending at NCLT Chandigarh, posing a direct threat to the company's going concern status and financial stability.
- Zero export revenue and no foreign exchange earnings — The company did not export any bicycles or components and had nil foreign exchange earnings, indicating complete dependence on the domestic market and loss of international diversification.
- Key managerial personnel turnover — The Whole Time Director and CFO resigned during the year, and a new CEO and CFO were appointed, which may disrupt strategic continuity and operational execution during a critical revival phase.
- No dividend and sustained losses — The company reported a net loss of â¹804 lacs compared to a profit of â¹951 lacs in the prior year, and declared no dividend, signaling deteriorating shareholder returns and capital erosion.
- Limited energy conservation and technology absorption — Due to unit closures and sub-optimal operations, the company could not pursue energy conservation or technology upgrades, hindering long-term competitiveness and cost efficiency.

- Business revival process — the Company is actively pursuing revival of its bicycle operations after minimal sales of ₹ 690 lacs in FY26.
